CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidney stones.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports sudden onset of right-sided back pain approximately one week ago while working in the barn moving hay. He initially thought the pain was from the activity but then developed associated diaphoresis and nausea, prompting him to see his PCP. A CT scan was ordered and confirmed the presence of a kidney stone. The pain radiated almost down to the groin. Since the initial onset, pain has occurred a couple more times but did not last as long. Patient denies current pain and has been straining urine as instructed without visualizing any stones. Denies hematuria or darkening of urine. Denies prior history of kidney stones.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever. Denies hematuria. Denies darkening of urine. Denies current pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Father has history of kidney stones.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works with horses in a barn, performing physical labor including moving hay.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs normal, no fever. Blood pressure and heart rate normal. Abdominal examination reveals no tenderness to palpation, no rebound or guarding. Costovertebral angle tenderness on right side.

RESULTS
CT scan shows a stone measuring 0.5 centimeters located in the proximal right ureter. No evidence of hydronephrosis. BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right ureteral kidney stone, 0.5 cm, proximal right ureter without obstruction. Plan: Increase fluid intake to facilitate passage of stone. Prescribe oxycodone 5 mg every 6-8 hours for pain, with acetaminophen for breakthrough pain. Continue urine straining. Obtain BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture to assess for infection; prescribe antibiotics if indicated based on urinalysis results. Follow-up in 1-2 weeks. If stone has not passed, discuss lithotripsy as treatment option.
